shortcut.name: CLI Tools
shortcut.description: Takes a natural-language description, asks the on-device model for the best matching macOS command line tool, verifies it with a shell script, records the lookup in the app's history, and optionally runs a checked command with the tool.

params.input_types_note: Collapsed in UI; 19 types total, only 'Apps' shown

params.prompt: What command line tool are you looking for?
params.placeholder: e.g. find which process is using port 8080

params.prompt_template:
Identify the single best macOS command-line utility for this task:

{{a2.Provided Input}}

Output exactly two lines:
First line: the executable's command name and nothing else. No label such as "Command:", no arguments, quotes or backticks.
Second line: one sentence explaining its purpose and basic usage.

No headings, markdown, introductory text, or additional lines.
Do not recommend destructive commands when a safer alternative is suitable.

actions.label: Get First Item from Split Text
Run Shell Script
actions.description: Extracts the command name from the model's first line (tolerating labels such as "Command:", list markers, backticks, arguments and trailing descriptions), validates it against an allowlist pattern, checks it is a real executable, and collects a summary and manual excerpt. First output line is always STATUS: OK, NOT_FOUND or INVALID. Always exits 0 so routing is done on the STATUS line.

params.script:
export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin

raw=$1
# First line only. The on-device model doesn't always follow the format, so tolerate:
#   a `backticked` command inside prose   ->  the backticked text
#   labels ("Command: lsof", "Line 1: lsof", "Tool name - lsof") and list markers ("1. lsof", "- lsof")
#   arguments or a trailing description ("lsof -i :8080", "lsof: lists open files")  ->  first word
# Case is preserved because some macOS tools are case-sensitive (SetFile, PlistBuddy).
line=$(printf '%s\n' "$raw" | head -n 1)
if [[ $line == *'`'?*'`'* ]]; then
  line=${line#*\`}
  line=${line%%\`*}
fi
tool=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | tr -d '*"'\' | sed -E \
  -e 's/^[[:space:]]+//' \
  -e 's/^([->]+|[0-9]+[.)])[[:space:]]+//' \
  -e 's/^([Ll]ine[[:space:]]*1|[Cc]ommand|[Tt]ool|[Ee]xecutable|[Uu]tility|[Pp]rogram|[Aa]nswer)([[:space:]]+[Nn]ame)?([[:space:]]*:|[[:space:]]+-)[[:space:]]*//' \
  -e 's/[[:space:]].*$//' \
  -e 's/[.,:;]+$//')

# Allowlist pattern: must start with a letter, digit or underscore (blocks option-like input such as -rf)
if [[ ${#tool} -eq 0 || ${#tool} -gt 64 || ! "$tool" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*$ ]]; then
  echo "STATUS: INVALID"
  echo "Reason: model output is not a plausible command name."
  echo "Model said: $(printf '%s\n' "$raw" | head -n 1)"
  exit 0
fi

# whence -p returns a real executable path only (not builtins, aliases or functions)
bin=$(whence -p "$tool" 2>/dev/null)
if [[ -z "$bin" ]]; then
  echo "STATUS: NOT_FOUND"
  echo "Tool: $tool"
  echo "Reason: not an executable on PATH (it may be a shell builtin or alias, or not installed)."
  exit 0
fi

echo "STATUS: OK"
echo "Tool: $tool"
echo "Path: $bin"

whatis_out=$(whatis "$tool" 2>/dev/null)
# Prefer the tool's own page ("ls(1) - list directory contents") over pages that merely mention it,
# such as the shell builtins page, which lists ls-F.
summary=$(printf '%s\n' "$whatis_out" | awk -v t="$tool(" 'index($0, t) == 1 { print; exit }')
[[ -z $summary ]] && summary=$(printf '%s\n' "$whatis_out" | awk -v t=", $tool(" 'index($0, t) && !/^builtin\(/ { print; exit }')
[[ -z $summary ]] && summary=$(printf '%s\n' "$whatis_out" | head -n 1)
if [[ -n "$summary" ]]; then
  echo "Summary: $summary"
else
  echo "Summary: unavailable (the whatis database may be missing; this does not mean the tool is invalid)"
fi
echo

if man -w "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  text=$(MANWIDTH=80 man "$tool" 2>/dev/null)
  if command -v col >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    text=$(printf '%s\n' "$text" | col -b)
  fi
  # Start at SYNOPSIS or DESCRIPTION rather than the header, up to 30 lines
  excerpt=$(printf '%s\n' "$text" | awk '/^(SYNOPSIS|DESCRIPTION)/{p=1} p{print; n++} n>=30{exit}')
  [[ -z "$excerpt" ]] && excerpt=$(printf '%s\n' "$text" | head -n 30)
  echo "Manual excerpt:"
  printf '%s\n' "$excerpt"
else
  echo "Manual: no man page found for $tool"
fi

actions.label: Save Lookup
actions.description: Records every lookup in the app's history database, the source of truth, including ones that fail verification. Status, tool and path are read from the STATUS/Tool/Path lines of a6.

then.label: Choose from menu

params.prompt: Run a command with this tool?

Run a Command.label: List
Run a Command.description: Bundles the lookup result and the model's response so the next script receives them as $1 and $2.

Run a Command.label: Suggest Command
Run a Command.description: Picks a `backticked` example from the model's explanation that starts with the verified tool, or falls back to the bare tool name.

params.script:
export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin

# $1 = lookup result (has a "Tool:" line), $2 = the model's full response.
tool=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/^Tool: //p' | head -n 1)

# Prefer a `backticked` example from the model's explanation that starts with the verified tool.
suggestion=""
rest=$2
while [[ $rest == *'`'?*'`'* ]]; do
  rest=${rest#*\`}
  span=${rest%%\`*}
  rest=${rest#*\`}
  if [[ ${span%% *} == "$tool" ]]; then
    suggestion=$span
    break
  fi
done
printf '%s\n' "${suggestion:-$tool}"

params.prompt: Run a command with this tool? Edit it first (replace placeholders such as <port>). It is checked before it runs, and the command and its result are saved to History. Cancel to finish without running anything.

Run a Command.label: Verify Command
Run a Command.description: Checks the command before anything runs: a single line with no shell operators, starting with the tool verified in a6 and still resolving to the same path, not a destructive or privileged tool, and without options that write files or run other programs. First output line is always STATUS: SAFE or STATUS: BLOCKED.

params.script:
export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin

# $1 = lookup result (has "Tool:" and "Path:" lines), $2 = the command the user confirmed.
# First output line is always STATUS: SAFE or STATUS: BLOCKED. Always exits 0.
tool=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/^Tool: //p' | head -n 1)
expected=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/^Path: //p' | head -n 1)
cmd=$(printf '%s' "$2" | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//')

block() {
  echo "STATUS: BLOCKED"
  echo "Command: $cmd"
  echo "Reason: $1"
  exit 0
}

[[ -z $tool ]] && block "the lookup step did not verify a tool."
[[ -z $cmd ]] && block "the command is empty."
[[ $cmd == *$'\n'* ]] && block "the command must be a single line."
(( ${#cmd} > 300 )) && block "the command is longer than 300 characters."

# One plain command only: no chaining, pipes, redirection, substitution or escapes.
if [[ $cmd == *[\;\&\|\<\>\`\$\(\)\{\}\\]* ]]; then
  [[ $cmd == *'<'*'>'* ]] && block "replace placeholders such as <port> with real values."
  block "shell operators ( ; & | < > \` \$ ( ) { } \\ ) are not allowed. Run one command with no pipes, redirection or substitution."
fi

# Split the way the run step will (zsh word splitting, quotes removed), never via eval.
words=("${(@Q)${(z)cmd}}")
[[ ${words[1]} != "$tool" ]] && block "the command must start with the verified tool \"$tool\", not \"${words[1]}\"."

# Re-verify the executable: it must still resolve to the same file the lookup found.
bin=$(whence -p "$tool" 2>/dev/null)
[[ -z $bin ]] && block "\"$tool\" is no longer an executable on PATH."
[[ -n $expected && $bin != "$expected" ]] && block "\"$tool\" now resolves to $bin instead of $expected."

# Tools that delete, overwrite, escalate privileges or change system state are never run.
case $tool in
  rm|rmdir|unlink|srm|shred|dd|truncate|mv|cp|ln|install|tee|chmod|chown|chgrp|chflags|xattr|\
  sudo|su|doas|login|passwd|kill|killall|pkill|shutdown|reboot|halt|launchctl|csrutil|nvram|\
  pmset|systemsetup|networksetup|scutil|fdesetup|diskutil|hdiutil|asr|tmutil|softwareupdate|\
  installer|pkgutil|pfctl|security|dscl|sysadminctl|spctl|osascript|open|crontab|at|mkfs*|newfs*)
    block "\"$tool\" can delete or change data or system settings, so this app won't run it." ;;
esac

# Options that make otherwise read-only tools write files or run other programs.
for (( i = 2; i <= ${#words}; i++ )); do
  w=${words[i]}
  case "$tool:$w" in
    find:-delete|find:-exec*|find:-ok*|find:-fprint*)
      block "find's $w option can delete files or run other commands." ;;
    sed:-i*|sed:--in-place*|perl:-i*|ruby:-i*)
      block "$tool $w edits files in place." ;;
    curl:-o|curl:-O|curl:--output*|curl:--remote-name*|curl:-T|curl:--upload-file*|wget:*)
      block "$tool $w would write or upload files." ;;
    defaults:write|defaults:delete|defaults:import|defaults:rename|git:push|git:reset|git:clean|brew:*)
      block "\"$tool $w\" changes settings, repositories or installed software." ;;
  esac
done

echo "STATUS: SAFE"
echo "Command: $cmd"
echo "Path: $bin"

then.label: Run Command
then.description: Repeats the safety check, then runs the approved command as an argument list (no eval) with no stdin, a 15-second limit and a 1 MB output cap. First output line is always EXIT: <code>, EXIT: TIMEOUT, EXIT: OUTPUT_LIMIT or EXIT: NOT_RUN.

params.script:
export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin
zmodload zsh/datetime

# $1 = the verify step's result. Only a command it marked SAFE is run, and the same checks are
# repeated here so this step can't run anything the verify step didn't approve.
# First output line is always EXIT: <code>, EXIT: TIMEOUT, EXIT: OUTPUT_LIMIT or EXIT: NOT_RUN. Always exits 0.
cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/^Command: //p' | head -n 1)
if [[ $1 != "STATUS: SAFE"* || -z $cmd || $cmd == *[\;\&\|\<\>\`\$\(\)\{\}\\]* ]]; then
  echo "EXIT: NOT_RUN"
  echo "Reason: the command was not verified as safe."
  exit 0
fi

# Run as an argument list (no eval), with no stdin, a 15-second limit and a 1 MB cap on any
# file it writes, including its own output (ulimit -f counts 512-byte blocks).
words=("${(@Q)${(z)cmd}}")
out=$(mktemp -t cli-tools)
start=$EPOCHREALTIME
( ulimit -f 2048; exec "${words[@]}" ) </dev/null >"$out" 2>&1 &
pid=$!
( sleep 15; kill -TERM $pid ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &
watcher=$!
wait $pid
code=$?
kill $watcher 2>/dev/null
elapsed=$(( EPOCHREALTIME - start ))

if (( elapsed >= 15 )); then
  echo "EXIT: TIMEOUT"
  echo "Note: stopped after 15 seconds (interactive or long-running commands aren't supported)."
elif (( code == 153 )); then
  echo "EXIT: OUTPUT_LIMIT"
  echo "Note: stopped after writing 1 MB of output."
else
  echo "EXIT: $code"
fi
printf 'Duration: %.1fs\n' $elapsed
echo "Output:"
lines=$(wc -l < "$out" | tr -d ' ')
if [[ ! -s $out ]]; then
  echo "(no output)"
else
  head -n 200 "$out" | cut -c 1-500
  (( lines > 200 )) && echo "… $(( lines - 200 )) more lines not shown"
fi
rm -f "$out"

notes: a6, a7 and a8 were added or reworked after the original screenshot (validation, STATUS routing, safer manual extraction).

a3's prompt and a6's name extraction were hardened after testing: the on-device model sometimes answers "command: lsof" or adds arguments, which the original cleanup rejected as INVALID. INVALID output now includes the model's first line.

1.4: the app's history database is the source of truth. a6r saves every lookup (including NOT_FOUND and INVALID); a8s9 and a8s12 attach each command, its verification and its result. Notes is no longer written by the pipeline; export a lookup to Notes from the History window instead.
Running a command: the model's example is suggested, you confirm or edit it, a8s6 verifies it, a8s8 re-checks and runs it. A non-zero exit or a blocked command shows an alert.
In the Shortcuts app, replace {{...}} placeholders with the real variables from the variable picker.
The original screenshot was cropped at the bottom; actions below the visible area, such as an End Menu, may exist.
Failed lookups stop with an alert. To keep them as diagnostic records instead, move the Save/Cancel menu out of the If's 'then' branch.
